title: Choose the visual world for Pragati's portfolio
question: The roll assigned The Practical File. Keep it, take the pick or the standard, or re-roll.

options.label: The Practical File
options.lineage: the B.Tech practical file and lab record every Indian engineer has submitted
options.thesis: Her portfolio is her practical file: each project is a signed experiment record, and the visitor is the examiner.
materials: ruled sheets with a red margin
options.viewport: The file lies open: on the left, the inside cover with her name label and a passport photo; on the right, the Index of experiments with a Sign column the visitor fills in.
options.risk: Reads as a school costume if the sheets are decoration instead of the real reading surface.

raised.raise: A 'Fair copy / Rough work' switch re-renders every record as an honest state: short for recruiters, full detail for engineers.
The Index is fully keyboard-driven: press 1 to 7 to open any experiment.
The file reads in fixed order, and the examiner's signature is earned at the Viva, which unlocks the email.
Every object is outlined, with no cast shadows: sheets separate by edges, staples, and tape.
The games use real physics and direct manipulation, not canned animation.
One red-ink thread runs the whole page, ticking each record and ending at the email.

options.label: The Hackathon Badge
options.lineage: SIH and NASA Space Apps event lanyards
options.thesis: Her identity as an event badge on a lanyard you can grab and swing; each project is an access level.
options.viewport: A badge hangs from the top edge on a lanyard with physics; her name, photo, and role are printed on it, with email on the reverse.
options.risk: This is the direction most dev portfolios land on: the physics lanyard has been widely copied since 2024.

options.label: Bitmap Type Specimen
options.thesis: Her name in coarse pixel letters at poster scale over dense columns.
options.viewport: A pixel headline towers over justified columns of her work.
options.case: Fuses poorly: recruiters and Indian engineers do not recognise Emigre, and the pixel display slows the ten-second scan.
options.risk: Reads as a type experiment, not an engineer's portfolio.
options.kept: An honest render-state toggle (bitmap vs smooth) became the Fair copy / Rough work switch.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: The portfolio as a BBS: numbered menus, door games, and 'leave mail for the sysop'.
options.viewport: An ANSI title screen pours in over a numbered menu.
options.case: Fuses partly: door games fit, but recruiters do not know BBS culture and it falls into the dark-terminal rut.
options.risk: Dark terminal is the most common dev-portfolio look.
options.kept: Complete keyboard operation with numbered exits.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Projects develop slowly into view under amber light.
options.viewport: A developer tray where her name emerges.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in her work or audience lives in a darkroom.
options.risk: Slow reveals fight the recruiter's ten-second scan.
options.kept: Fixed stations in order with a commitment point.

options.label: Chaekgeori Shelf
options.thesis: Projects as objects on a cabinet that opens toward you.
options.viewport: A shelf grid in reverse perspective.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to her audience or culture.
options.kept: Outlined objects with no cast shadows.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.thesis: Rain falls by cloud colour; visitors paint gravity.
options.viewport: A dusk garden with coloured rain.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a toy with no product truth for a backend engineer.
options.kept: Real physics with direct manipulation in the games.

options.label: Rain-Night City
options.thesis: A city from blue hour to dawn, traffic as data.
options.viewport: A skyline with amber transit lines.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neon night is the dark-dev rut, and clarity drops.
options.kept: One continuous light journey across the page.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio: big name, short bio, project cards, contact icons, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role at left, photo at right, project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of portfolios by design.
